explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - UI-TARS is an open-source, multimodal GUI-automation tool built around a vision-language model.  
   - It is not a full-stack web app but a library/toolchain that:  
     • Sends screenshots or observations to a remote model endpoint (Hugging Face)  
     • Receives text-based action plans  
     • Parses and executes those actions on a target GUI (desktop/mobile/emulator)  

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level:  
     • README*.md, LICENSE, paper PDFs (documentation)  
     • codes/ – core scripts  
     • data/ – sample messages and training examples (testing, dev)  
     • figures/ – icons, diagrams for the paper  
   - codes/ breakdown:  
     • prompts.py – prompt templates (COMPUTER_USE, MOBILE_USE, GROUNDING)  
     • action_parser.py – converts model output into pyautogui calls  
     • utils.py – shared helper functions (e.g., coordinate transforms)  
     • inference_test.py – scripts for local inference tests  
   - Configuration & deployment:  
     • README_deploy.md – instructions for setting up a Hugging Face endpoint  

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Describes a two-stage runtime:  
     1) Deployment & inference on remote model  
     2) Post-processing to yield executable GUI actions  
   - Mentions coordinate processing via README_coordinates.md  
   - Lists benchmarks and model scales (72B, 7B, 1.5)  

4. System design diagram instructions  
   a. Main components  
     1) Client / Orchestration Layer  
        – Inference script (inference_test.py or custom client)  
        – Prompt builder (prompts.py)  
     2) Model Serving Layer  
        – Hugging Face Endpoint (UI-TARS-1.5-7B or other scale)  
     3) Post-Processing Layer  
        – Action parser (action_parser.py)  
        – Coordinate conversion (utils.py + README_coordinates guide)  
     4) Execution Layer  
        – pyautogui / mobile-automation library  
        – Target environment (desktop OS, emulator)  
     5) Data & Testing  
        – Sample messages (data/)  
        – Inference tests (inference_test.py)  

   b. Relationships & interactions  
     1) Orchestration Layer captures a screenshot / environment state  
     2) Uses prompt templates to format input  
     3) Sends prompt+image context to Model Serving Layer (HTTP/RPC)  
     4) Receives “Thought” + “Action” strings  
     5) Passes to Post-Processing Layer for parsing into code-level commands  
     6) Utility functions handle coordinate normalization  
     7) Execution Layer invokes GUI actions on the target system  
     8) Optionally loop with new observation for multi-step tasks  

   c. Architectural patterns & principles  
     - “Pipeline” / “Chain-of-responsibility”: each layer transforms data  
     - Clear separation of concerns: prompting, inference, parsing, execution  
     - Pluggability: you can swap out model endpoints or change parsing logic  
     - Testability: sample inputs in data/ and inference test scripts  

   d. Key technologies & libraries  
     - Python 3.x  
     - Hugging Face Inference API (model serving)  
     - pyautogui (desktop automation)  
     - Emulator APIs or ADB (mobile)  
     - JSON for data interchange  
     - OpenAI-style prompt templates  

5. Guidelines for tailoring the diagram  
   - Since this is an automation tool, emphasize the linear flow rather than a client-server web architecture.  
   - Show the “model endpoint” as an external service box.  
   - Group code modules into logical layers (Orchestrator, Model, Parser, Executor).  
   - Annotate where tests/data live and how they feed into the pipeline.  

6. Diagram elements to include  
   - Components as labeled boxes (Orchestrator, Model, Parser, Executor, Data Store)  
   - Directional arrows for data flow:  
     • Screenshot → Prompt Builder → Model Endpoint → Parser → Executor  
   - Color coding:  
     • Blue for computation layers (Prompt, Parser)  
     • Green for external services (Model endpoint)  
     • Orange for side resources (data/, figures/)  
   - Shapes or icons:  
     • Cylinder icon for data files  
     • Cloud icon for remote model  
     • Document icon for prompts.py  

7. Emphasis on detail  
   - Capture each Python script’s role in the pipeline  
   - Show coordinate conversion as a sub-component of the Parser layer  
   - Don’t omit test scripts or the deployment guide—they inform how to spin up the system  

By following these steps and grouping the project’s scripts and resources into the layers above, you’ll produce a clear, accurate system design diagram that fully represents UI-TARS’s architecture.  
</explanation>
